title: Final Capstone: Build the Campus Events API
summary: Build a complete local Express API for campus events with SQLite persistence, read routes, filters, mutations, validation, and resilient error responses.

sketchBlocks.title: Build one complete API contract from server shell to persistent service
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The Campus Event Explorer needs one dependable backend boundary.

You will build the full service cumulatively: collection and resource reads, filtering, validation, creation, partial updates, deletion, consistent client errors, SQLite persistence, a final safe server-error boundary, and deterministic localhost verification.

The goal is not to invent a new contract at each milestone. Every step preserves the working responsibilities that came before it.

sketchBlocks.title: HTTP, validation, repository, and persistence each have a clear job
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
As the service grows, keep responsibilities separated.

Routes translate HTTP input and choose statuses. The validator decides whether client-supplied event fields are acceptable. Repository functions own SQL and return application data. SQLite stores event rows in `data/events.db`. The final error middleware catches unexpected failures without exposing internal details.

This separation lets the persistence layer change without breaking the client-facing API contract.

sketchBlocks.title: Finish by proving success and error outcomes through localhost
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The final milestone checks the service through deterministic requests to `127.0.0.1`.

Verify the collection, filtering, one-resource detail, successful creation, rejected invalid input, partial update, deletion, missing-resource handling, and the safe unexpected-failure response. Close both the server and database after the checks complete.

A finished capstone should demonstrate that all earlier responsibilities now work together in one coherent local service.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 1: Create the server shell
quizDraft.prompt: Create the Express app, register JSON middleware, and start the service on `127.0.0.1:3000`.
quizDraft.hint: Keep the first milestone focused on the local server boundary.

help.concept: The capstone starts with a deterministic Express service that later milestones extend.
help.hint_1: Create one Express application and register the JSON parser before routes.
help.hint_2: Use the local host and course port for the listener.

quizDraft.starterCode: // Build the Campus Events API in server.js.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 2: Model the event resource
quizDraft.prompt: Add three deterministic starter events in memory. Every event must use the same `id`, `title`, and `category` shape.
quizDraft.hint: Keep the resource shape small and consistent; persistence arrives later in the capstone.

help.concept: A stable resource shape gives every route the same event contract.
help.hint_1: Use numeric ids and string title/category fields.
help.hint_2: Keep the starter data deterministic for later localhost checks.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 3: List events
quizDraft.prompt: Implement `GET /api/events` and return the complete event collection with status `200` JSON.
quizDraft.hint: Do not add filtering yet; this milestone establishes the collection route.

help.concept: A collection route returns a predictable JSON array at one stable path.
help.hint_1: Register the GET route for the events collection.
help.hint_2: Return the current event collection as JSON.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 4: Filter events
quizDraft.prompt: Extend `GET /api/events` with an optional `category` query parameter. When present, return only matching events; otherwise return the full collection.
quizDraft.hint: Read the filter from `req.query` and leave the source collection unchanged.

help.concept: Optional query filters refine a collection without changing the resource route.
help.hint_1: Use the query value only to choose the returned collection.
help.hint_2: Preserve the unfiltered behavior when no category is provided.

sourceChecks.message: Filter the collection without mutating it.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 5: Read one event
quizDraft.prompt: Implement `GET /api/events/:id`. Normalize the route id, find the matching event, and return it with status `200`.
quizDraft.hint: This milestone adds identity lookup; missing-resource behavior comes next.

help.concept: A resource route maps one route parameter to one event identity.
help.hint_1: Convert the route parameter to the same type used by stored ids.
help.hint_2: Find the event before sending the success response.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 6: Handle missing reads
quizDraft.prompt: Preserve the resource route and return status `404` JSON `{ error: "Event not found" }` when the id has no match.
quizDraft.hint: Branch before the success response when the lookup returns no event.

help.concept: A stable not-found outcome is part of the client-facing API contract.
help.hint_1: Keep the same resource path and success behavior.
help.hint_2: Only the missing branch should produce the client error.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 7: Validate event input
quizDraft.prompt: Add one reusable `validateEventInput` helper for create and partial-update data. It should report invalid `title` and `category` fields without mutating state.
quizDraft.hint: Support both full validation and partial validation so PATCH can reuse the same helper.

help.concept: One reusable validator keeps accepted event fields consistent across create and update operations.
help.hint_2: Partial validation checks a field only when the client supplied it.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 8: Create events
quizDraft.prompt: Implement `POST /api/events`. Generate the next local id, append one event, and return the created representation with status `201`.
quizDraft.hint: This milestone establishes creation; invalid create rejection is added next.

help.concept: POST creates one resource and returns the representation clients can use immediately.
help.hint_1: Generate an id from the current deterministic collection.
help.hint_2: Push the new object once and return that same object.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 9: Reject invalid creates
quizDraft.prompt: Call `validateEventInput(req.body)` before creating an event. Return status `400` with `{ error: "Validation failed", fields }` when validation finds problems, without mutating the collection.
quizDraft.hint: The invalid branch must return before id generation and `events.push(...)`.

help.concept: Validation protects state by stopping malformed creates before mutation.
help.hint_1: Run the reusable validator against the parsed body.
help.hint_2: Keep the valid create path and `201` response unchanged.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 10: Patch events
quizDraft.prompt: Implement `PATCH /api/events/:id`. Reuse partial validation, update only supplied allowed fields, return `404` for a missing target, `400` for invalid supplied values, and `200` with the updated event on success.
quizDraft.hint: Find the target first, validate supplied fields, then mutate only fields that are present.

help.concept: PATCH preserves unspecified fields while applying validated partial changes.
help.hint_1: Call the validator with partial mode enabled.
help.hint_2: Use explicit undefined checks before changing each allowed property.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 11: Delete events
quizDraft.prompt: Implement `DELETE /api/events/:id`. Return `404` for a missing id, remove exactly one matching event, and return status `204` on success.
quizDraft.hint: Find the target index before mutating the array.

help.concept: DELETE should remove exactly one identified resource while preserving every read/update route.
help.hint_1: Treat the missing index sentinel as not found.
help.hint_2: Use `splice(index, 1)` only after the target exists.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 12: Unify client errors
quizDraft.prompt: Add `sendError(res, status, message, extra)` and use it for validation and not-found responses so `400` and `404` outcomes share one understandable JSON convention.
quizDraft.hint: Keep domain decisions in routes; use the helper only for repeated response formatting.

help.concept: A focused response helper keeps client errors consistent without hiding route logic.
help.hint_1: The helper should always include an `error` key.
help.hint_2: Allow validation responses to add the `fields` array through extra data.

sourceChecks.message: Use the helper for missing resources.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 13: Persist events with SQLite
quizDraft.prompt: Replace the temporary event array with `data/events.db`. Initialize the events table, seed only an empty table, move CRUD into parameterized repository functions, and keep all existing routes/status/error behavior stable.
quizDraft.hint: This is a storage-layer replacement, not an HTTP-contract rewrite.

help.concept: SQLite persistence belongs behind repository functions so clients see the same API behavior across restarts.
help.hint_1: Use placeholders for all client-supplied database values.
help.hint_2: Keep route handlers focused on HTTP input, validation, and response outcomes.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 14: Handle unexpected failures
quizDraft.prompt: Add a final Express error handler that logs unexpected failures server-side and returns status `500` JSON `{ error: "Internal server error" }` without exposing implementation details. Add the local verification-failure route used only to exercise this boundary.
quizDraft.hint: Register the verification route before the final error middleware, and register the error middleware before the listener.

help.concept: A final error boundary protects clients from internal details while preserving server-side diagnostics.
help.hint_1: Use the four-argument Express error-middleware signature.
help.hint_2: Return only the stable public error message to the client.

sourceChecks.message: Add the local failure verification route.
Use the safe public error message.

quizDraft.title: Milestone 15: Verify the complete contract
quizDraft.prompt: Keep the complete persistent API. From the local listen callback, verify list, filter, detail, valid create, invalid create, patch, delete, `404`, and the safe `500` response; log each status and close the server/database.
quizDraft.hint: Use only requests to the service running on `127.0.0.1`.

help.concept: Final verification proves the complete HTTP contract, persistent storage, validation, CRUD, and resilient error behavior work together.
help.hint_1: Create a real stored event before exercising PATCH and DELETE.
help.hint_2: Include the local failure-verification endpoint so the final error middleware is exercised too.
